chapter: Society work, Camilla Todd and Storyville
title: How he fell ill and gave up the horn; insurance work
summary: He describes doctors, the nerve trouble in his lip, and a sick policyholder's symptoms that frightened him.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: you know, it's like if you was in the woods, you know. You know, that man still could play that funk before he's singing that. When we got through, I'm telling you, those people, bah bah bah bah bah bah bah bah bah. I told Chick, I said Chick, I got him. Will your doctor let you play anymore? Well he didn't stop me because I had to stop. You see, on the last day, you see the doctor tried to stop me but he couldn't. You see they had me to go to Dr. Hava in the Chicka building on Canal Street where I got Chauveti's place now. Well Dr. Hava was one of the finest positions you had in the city of New York. And those people did everything possible to see that I would get well, you see. But when I'd blow that instrument, it looked like if you'd take a razor, you know, and cut right here. And you know how that happened? I couldn't sleep in the daytime and I used to play day and night. Oh and this was in the nerves. That's right. The nerves acting up. They claimed that it was weeks planned right here. And the doctor said they never knew of anybody who lived with that. Is that right? But believe me, I got frightened only once, the whole time I was sick. I went to an insurance business after I left the music. And on my route, when I got on Dupree and Broad, they had one of my insurer there. He used to work for the New Orleans Railway Light Company, one of the porters there. And he was giving me the same symptom that I had, you see. And the next day when I went to collect there again, they had unburied him. So you just started taking care of yourself. But I was praying to the Blessed Mother, I said, let me get away from God. I'll never put that in my lip no more.
